name: lightforge
description: Linux Native World of Warcraft / Battle.net Launcher
readme_summary: Lightforge is a native Linux client for World of Warcraft and other Battle.net games. It allows users to install, patch, verify, and launch World of Warcraft directly without the official Battle.net client, using reimplemented Blizzard distribution protocols in Rust. For other Battle.net games, it manages a single Battle.net prefix and launches the official client.
key_features: Native Linux launcher for World of Warcraft
Installs, patches, verifies, and launches WoW without Battle.net client
Reimplements TACT, NGDP, and CASC protocols in Rust
Compatible with Battle.net's adopted game folders
Manages a single Battle.net prefix for other Blizzard games
Provides a graphical user interface
primary_use_case: To provide a seamless and native experience for playing World of Warcraft and other Battle.net games on Linux systems, bypassing the need for the official Battle.net client for WoW and simplifying the management of other Blizzard titles.
cover_image_prompt: A skilled artisan in a workshop, meticulously crafting a detailed miniature castle (World of Warcraft) from raw digital blueprints and glowing energy streams (Blizzard protocols). Tools on the workbench show snippets of Rust code and UI elements. In the background, a larger, more generic city gate (Battle.net) stands, with the artisan handing off smaller, pre-packaged parcels (other games) to a waiting courier. The overall mood is one of creation and efficient management, with a clean, modern aesthetic and subtle digital particle effects. The style should be a 3D isometric illustration with a focus on clear visual storytelling and a vibrant, tech-inspired color palette.

name: maple-videos
description: A open-source Video Hosting platform for people who wnats to self host thier own videos
readme_summary: Maple-videos is an open-source, self-hosted video hosting platform that allows users to upload, transcode, and serve their own videos using a built-in player. It aims to provide an alternative to corporate video platforms by keeping user data on their own servers.
key_features: Video uploads with size limits and format checks
Real video validation using ffprobe
Background transcoding to HLS with FFmpeg
Built-in player powered by hls.js
Video list on homepage
No tracking, no accounts, no third parties
primary_use_case: Self-hosting and serving personal video content without reliance on third-party platforms.
cover_image_prompt: A medieval scribe meticulously copying ancient scrolls onto fresh parchment, but the scrolls are digital video files and the parchment is a modern, sleek server rack. The scribe uses a quill that glows with digital light, transforming raw video data (represented as tangled threads) into organized, flowing HLS streams (smooth, glowing ribbons). In the background, a small, stylized monitor displays the maple-videos logo and a simple, clean interface showing a list of videos. The scene is set in a cozy, well-lit workshop with subtle digital particles floating in the air, emphasizing a blend of traditional craftsmanship and modern technology. The overall style is a 3D isometric illustration with a warm, inviting color palette.

name: mango
description: A self-hosted manga and manhwa reader that runs Mihon extensions
readme_summary: Mango is a self-hosted manga and manhwa reader built with Rust. It leverages Mihon-compatible extensions to access content from various sources and can also read local files. The application is designed to be lightweight, with a single Rust binary for the server and web UI, and extensions running in a separate, on-demand process.
key_features: Self-hosted manga and manhwa reader
Runs Mihon-compatible extensions
Reads from online sources via extensions
Reads from local files
Lightweight Rust binary
Extensions run in a separate process
primary_use_case: Self-hosting a manga and manhwa reader application that aggregates content from online sources (via extensions) and local files, offering a centralized and customizable reading experience.
cover_image_prompt: A stylized, open book with pages transforming into digital streams of manga panels and covers. A friendly, anthropomorphic robot character, subtly branded with the 'Mango' logo, is carefully organizing these streams into neat shelves within a cozy, self-contained digital library. Small, glowing icons representing different manga sources float around, and a subtle progress bar indicates content being 'read' or 'cataloged'. The overall scene should evoke a sense of organized digital content management and personal library building, rendered in a clean, 3D isometric illustration style with a warm, inviting color palette.

name: materialfy
description: Native Spotify desktop client in Material 3 Expressive (Rust + librespot + Qt Quick)
readme_summary: Materialfy is a native desktop client for Spotify built using Rust and Qt Quick, offering a Material 3 Expressive user interface. It provides a streamlined music listening experience on Windows and Linux, with experimental support for macOS. The client integrates audio playback via librespot and dynamically adapts interface colors to the current track's album art.
key_features: Native desktop Spotify client
Material 3 Expressive UI
Built with Rust and Qt Quick
Uses librespot for audio playback
Dynamic color theming based on album art
Available for Windows and Linux
Experimental macOS support
Automatic update checks
primary_use_case: To provide a modern, visually appealing, and native desktop experience for listening to Spotify music, distinct from the official web-based client.
cover_image_prompt: A stylized, modern music player interface, resembling a sleek, glowing digital console, is at the center. From this console, vibrant streams of musical notes and abstract sound waves flow outwards, transforming into colorful album art covers that float around it. A subtle, almost invisible layer of code or data particles emanates from the console, hinting at the underlying technology. The overall mood is clean, futuristic, and artistic, with a focus on the seamless integration of music, visuals, and user experience. The 'Materialfy' name is subtly integrated into the console's design. 3D isometric illustration style with soft, ambient lighting and a sophisticated color palette.

name: SnapBack-Rebootless
description: A Windows app that remembers your preferred set of apps, monitors memory usage, and closes extra programs with your approval, without rebooting.
readme_summary: SnapBack is a Windows application designed to restore your system to a desired baseline state without requiring a reboot. It intelligently identifies and closes applications that have been opened since the baseline was set, allowing them to save work politely, and optionally includes a deep memory cleanup feature.
key_features: Records application states as baselines or named profiles.
Monitors session drift from the baseline.
Groups processes into applications for accurate comparison.
Politely closes applications, allowing them to save work.
Offers an optional deep memory cleanup for file cache.
Provides a preview and dry-run mode before closing applications.
Reports on applications that did not close and allows manual intervention.
Displays before and after system state (apps, processes, memory).
primary_use_case: To manage and reset a Windows session to a clean, predefined state by closing unwanted applications without rebooting, thereby freeing up system resources and reducing clutter.
cover_image_prompt: A meticulous librarian carefully organizing a vast library after a busy day. Books representing open applications are neatly placed back on shelves, while a few stray books are gently removed and placed in a 'to be filed' cart. The librarian has a serene expression, indicating a controlled and polite process. Subtle digital elements like glowing data streams and small UI overlays showing 'Session Drift: Low' and 'Memory Freed: 7.1 GB' are integrated into the scene. The background shows a clean, organized digital workspace. The overall mood is calm and efficient. The art style is a 3D isometric illustration with a clean, modern aesthetic and a soft, inviting color palette.

name: Claude-Mods
readme_summary: Claude Mods enhances the Claude Code AI assistant by providing plugins that help users manage context limits, continue long tasks after chat resets, organize multiple sessions, and monitor resource usage. These mods aim to improve productivity and workflow within the Claude Code environment.
key_features: Context, limits, and reset timers displayed next to the chat (CTX)
Continue long tasks after chat clearing using saved summaries (Handoff)
Multiple parallel sessions for project work (Threads)
Centralized panel for all dialogues with search and switching (Session Hub)
Confirmation before deleting files and other dangerous actions (Delete Guard)
primary_use_case: Enhancing the functionality and user experience of Claude Code through installable plugins for better task management, session organization, and resource monitoring.
cover_image_prompt: A wise old librarian meticulously organizing a vast, multi-layered library. Each layer represents a different 'session' or 'thread' of a complex project. The librarian uses a magical magnifying glass (CTX) to see the 'knowledge limits' and 'time until reset' of each section, displayed as glowing runes. When a section is 'cleared' (Handoff), the librarian quickly creates a detailed summary scroll to ensure the knowledge isn't lost. In the background, a 'Session Hub' acts as a central control panel, showing all library sections. The overall mood is one of organized productivity and enhanced understanding within a digital, ethereal library. 3D isometric illustration style, clean lines, vibrant but calm color palette.
